svg.title: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Pilot
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Pilot; subtitle: Build operating evidence now; allow 3–12 months for the first deal.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values mark milestone end days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. The sprint establishes a functioning pilot and decision evidence, not a promised signed client or enterprise contract. Outreach requires the relevant checks to be completed and, when acting for a client, documented client authorization.; caption: Finish with traceable account records, tested acceptance logic, a reconciled pilot ledger, and a cash-backed continuation decision.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Select one sub-niche and define the billable opportunity.; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Interview prospective buyers, document the ideal customer profile, define retainer deliverables and acceptance criteria, review sector restrictions, and build a cash forecast around the 3–12 month first-deal range.; label: Days 8-14; value: Configure the CRM, provenance records, and suppression workflows.; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Implement client-account identifiers, source timestamps, contact restrictions, acceptance fields, and invoice references. Test scheduling, duplicate detection, opt-out handling, and access controls using clearly labeled test records.; label: Days 15-21; value: Run a narrow pilot with documented outreach authority.; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Launch a capacity-limited account cohort only after pre-flight checks. If no client is signed, test the agency's own acquisition workflow instead of claiming client delivery. Record replies, attended meetings, labor hours, and actual cash spend.; label: Days 22-30; value: Audit cohort evidence and decide the next funded iteration.; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Review acceptance failures, duplicate claims, response quality, collection terms, and client concentration exposure. Reconcile any earned fees with the ledger, update the cash forecast, and expand only when workload and available runway support the added commitments.

text.title: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Pilot
text.tspan: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Pilot

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Select one sub-niche and define the billable opportunity.; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Interview prospective buyers, document the ideal customer profile, define retainer deliverables and acceptance criteria, review sector restrictions, and build a cash forecast around the 3–12 month first-deal range.

text.title: Select one sub-niche and define the billable opportunity.

circle.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Configure the CRM, provenance records, and suppression workflows.; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Implement client-account identifiers, source timestamps, contact restrictions, acceptance fields, and invoice references. Test scheduling, duplicate detection, opt-out handling, and access controls using clearly labeled test records.

text.title: Configure the CRM, provenance records, and suppression workflows.

circle.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Run a narrow pilot with documented outreach authority.; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Launch a capacity-limited account cohort only after pre-flight checks. If no client is signed, test the agency's own acquisition workflow instead of claiming client delivery. Record replies, attended meetings, labor hours, and actual cash spend.

text.title: Run a narrow pilot with documented outreach authority.

circle.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Audit cohort evidence and decide the next funded iteration.; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Review acceptance failures, duplicate claims, response quality, collection terms, and client concentration exposure. Reconcile any earned fees with the ledger, update the cash forecast, and expand only when workload and available runway support the added commitments.

text.title: Audit cohort evidence and decide the next funded iteration.

Assumptions: Numeric values mark milestone end days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. The sprint establishes a functioning pilot and decision evidence, not a promised signed client or enterprise contract. Outreach requires the relevant checks to be completed and, when acting for a client, documented client authorization.
